extractor.note: Whole file grep-counted for the theme's search terms plus 'Wesensschau', 'eidetic', 'eidos' and 'essentia': 'Wesensschau' and 'eidetic' occur nowhere; 'eidos' occurs once, at § 13, of the pure look in which intraworldly beings are encountered. Closely read § 9 (lines 282-305); §§ 6, 4 and 44 were keyword-scanned. This is the second commentary in the corpus on the same primary text as heidegger-sein-und-zeit-commentary, and the two records should be read together.

coverage_note: Covers § 9 (the theme of the analytic of Dasein) in full, and records the single occurrence of eidos at § 13. The rest of the Introduction and both Divisions were keyword-scanned only. Unlike heidegger-sein-und-zeit-commentary, this commentary never names the Wesensschau.

units.claim: The essence of Dasein is said to lie in its having-to-be, its what-being (essentia) being graspable only from its being (existentia), if at all.
units.quote: the "essence" of this being lies in its *having-to-be* (*Zu-sein*). The what-being (*essentia*) of this being must, insofar as one can speak of it at all, be grasped from its Being (*existentia*).

units.claim: The title existence is said not to have the ontological meaning of the traditional existentia, which means presence-at-hand, a mode of being that does not belong to Dasein.
units.quote: *existentia* ontologically means as much as presence-at-hand (*Vorhandenheit*), a mode of Being that essentially does not belong to the being of the character of Dasein

units.claim: The commentary glosses the formula as a radical departure from all substance-metaphysics: Dasein has no fixed nature, its what being its how.
units.quote: This is a radical departure from all substance-metaphysics: Dasein has no fixed nature. Its "what" just *is* its "how" — its manner of existing.

units.claim: The characters exhibitable in Dasein are said not to be present-at-hand properties but in each case possible ways for it to be, all its so-being being primarily being.
units.quote: The characters exhibitable in this being are therefore not present-at-hand "properties" of a present-at-hand being that "looks" thus-and-so, but in each case possible ways for it to be, and only that.

units.claim: Dasein can have lost itself or not yet won itself only insofar as it is by its essence possible authentic, that is, belonging to itself.
units.quote: insofar as it is by its essence possible authentic — that is, belonging to itself

units.claim: A mode of being toward the world is said to let intraworldly beings be encountered only in their pure look, rendered eidos, on the basis of which an explicit looking-at becomes possible.
units.quote: which lets intraworldly beings be encountered only in their pure look (*eidos*)

absences.expected_because: The section suspends the essentia/existentia pair for Dasein and so settles what 'essence' may mean in this commentary; the parallel commentary on the same text, heidegger-sein-und-zeit-commentary, reaches the Wesensschau at its § 31, so the question is whether this one does anywhere.
absences.note: It does not: 'Wesensschau' and 'eidetic' occur nowhere in this commentary, and its single 'eidos' is the pure look of § 13, not Husserl's. Recorded so the two commentaries on Sein und Zeit can be told apart on this theme.
